claims.text: Introducing SRO precipitates into crystalline silicon will decrease its lattice thermal conductivity.
Intrinsic crystalline silicon is a semiconductor whose heat conduction is primarily phononic under the proposed conditions.
Controlled thermal processing or alloying can produce uniformly distributed nanoscale SRO precipitates in a silicon matrix.
Phonon conduction dominates in the proposed room-temperature or selected temperature regime.
The electronic contribution to heat conduction in the proposed silicon samples is minimal.
SRO precipitates act as discrete phonon-scattering centers in the silicon lattice.
Increased phonon scattering reduces the phonon mean free path.
A reduced phonon mean free path lowers lattice thermal conductivity relative to pristine silicon.
Silicon containing SRO precipitates will exhibit measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than pristine silicon.
The magnitude of the thermal-conductivity reduction scales with SRO precipitate density.
The proposed effect should be notable in insulating or intrinsic-semiconductor systems dominated by lattice heat transport.
The effect may be less discernible in materials with substantial electronic heat conduction.
Precipitate size, distribution, and density affect phonon-scattering efficiency and therefore the quantitative conductivity reduction.
